newsitem.title: CANADA: Numac to increase spending in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Numac to increase spending in 1997.

text.p: Numac Energy Inc said on Thursday it would boost its exploration and development spending to C$130 million in 1997 from C$110 million in 1996.
Numac said the budget increase reflected "excellent prospects" that were developed through its new strategic plan announced in May.
It said its capital program would be dominated by projects at Manatokan in Alberta and the Tommy Lakes-Sliver-Martin Corridor in northeast British Columbia.
About C$65 million was earmarked for the two areas for drilling, completions and facilities, Numac said.
The rest of the budget would be spent on light oil development projects in southeast Saskatchewan and high-impact exploration in west-central Alberta and northeast B.C., it said.
In total, the budget envisaged participating in 225 gross (160 net) wells in 1997.

At the 100 percent-owned Manatokan heavy oil property, Numac expected to drill 100 wells and build a central battery with a capacity of 7,000 barrels a day. Production from the area was estimated at 4,500 barrels a day by the end of 1997 and 10,000 by the end of 1998.
At Tommy Lakes-Sliver-Martin, the company aimed to spend C$25 million to develop natural gas infrastructure and participate in 20 multi-zone wells, it said.
